review_notes: I read the whole file. It declares no simp lemmas or attributes. Its simp use is limited to two `simp_rw [hLuid …]` / `simp_rw [hLDid …]` calls, and I found no loops or competing rules there. I checked the `vlSlab` definition and `vlSlab_measure` in VorticityLocalizedEnergyWeakTime.lean. I grepped for a bridge lemma between `spaceTimeSet univ (Ioo _ _)` and `vlSlab` and found none; the `rfl` `have` is repeated in two LPS files. I did not check whether `spaceTimeSet` has simp lemmas elsewhere. This finding is a modest interface gap, not a simplifier failure. I could not run Lean, so nothing here was tested.

have hslab : spaceTimeSet (Set.univ : Set Vec3) (Ioo t₀ T) = vlSlab t₀ T := rfl
  rw [hslab] at hMemU hMemDu hMemD2u hMemDtu
findings.problem: The two slab notions `spaceTimeSet univ (Ioo a b)` and `vlSlab a b` are identified only by a local `rfl` `have`, then applied with `rw … at` to four hypotheses. The same `have` is copied in LocalStrongKineticEnergy.lean. No named lemma bridges the two forms, and none is available to `simp`/`simp only`/`rw`. The main theorem is stated with `spaceTimeSet` (lines 192–199), while the supporting lemmas are stated with `vlSlab`. Every caller therefore has to rebuild this conversion by hand. A reader also cannot see which of the two forms is the canonical one.
findings.proposed_change: Add one named lemma next to the `vlSlab` definition: `theorem spaceTimeSet_univ_Ioo_eq_vlSlab (a b : ℝ) : spaceTimeSet (Set.univ : Set Vec3) (Ioo a b) = vlSlab a b := rfl`. Mark it `@[simp]` only if `vlSlab` is chosen as the canonical form. Otherwise use it only through `simp only [...]`/`rw`. Then replace both local `have hslab … := rfl` copies with `simp only [spaceTimeSet_univ_Ioo_eq_vlSlab] at hMemU hMemDu hMemD2u hMemDtu`. The `rfl` proof is safe and the orientation is explicit.
findings.benefit: One canonical, documented rewrite replaces two duplicated local `rfl` facts. Downstream slab proofs can normalise to `vlSlab`, where the integral and measure lemmas such as `vlSlab_measure` are stated. The conversion also no longer depends on definitional unfolding at each use.
